mechanism_narrative: Sustained week-on-week improvement in WORKPLACES mobility (from -73.7% to -68.3% over t-1w to t-0w) signals resumption of commuting patterns. This drives incidental retail visits during work trips, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved 5.4 percentage points from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days does not exceed the mean over the last 28 days (-82.9%), or WORKPLACES reverses by more than 3 percentage points in week t+1w.

mechanism_narrative: Accelerating recovery in TRANSIT mobility (from -77.9% to -74.1%, a 3.8 point improvement) indicates growing public confidence in movement. This confidence spillover increases discretionary retail visits independent of workplace reopening, driving RETAIL_REC higher over four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved 3.8 percentage points from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days remains below -80%, or TRANSIT mobility reverses to below -75% in any of the next two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM mobility exceeds -50% (currently -53.0%, approaching threshold), consumers gain confidence in public spaces and shift from essential-only to discretionary shopping. This cross-category behavioral shift drives RETAIL_REC recovery if GROCERY_PHARM crosses -50% within two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM at -53.0%, within 3 points of -50% threshold
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM does not cross -50% within two weeks, or RETAIL_REC fails to improve by at least 5 percentage points in the week following the crossing.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous recovery across WORKPLACES and TRANSIT (both improving 3-5 points week-on-week) signals coordinated policy easing. When both series improve together, retail landlords and merchants increase operating hours and staffing, enabling higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improve by >2 percentage points in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved 5.4 points, TRANSIT improved 3.8 points from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed -75%, or either WORKPLACES or TRANSIT reverses by more than 2 points in week t+1w.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent gap between RESIDENTIAL mobility (29.0%) and RETAIL_REC (-82.9%) indicates people remain home-bound despite some workplace/transit recovery. If RESIDENTIAL mobility declines further below 25%, it signals accelerating exit from homes, driving retail visits upward over the next week.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL at 29.0%, declining from 31.0% at t-1w
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL does not fall below 25% within one week, or RETAIL_REC fails to improve by at least 3 percentage points in week t+1w.

mechanism_narrative: Parks mobility remains severely depressed (-94.7%), indicating outdoor recreation restrictions remain binding. If PARKS mobility improves by more than 5 points within two weeks, it signals policy shift enabling outdoor activity, which substitutes for indoor retail. This substitution effect suppresses RETAIL_REC recovery.
candidate_trigger: PARKS improves by >5 percentage points in a single week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS at -94.7%, showing minimal week-on-week improvement
failure_condition: PARKS does not improve by >5 points within two weeks, or RETAIL_REC increases by more than 5 percentage points despite PARKS improvement.

mechanism_narrative: Convergence of GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC recovery signals unified consumer confidence in retail environments. When both series improve together by >3 points week-on-week, it indicates merchants are reopening across categories, creating network effects that accelerate RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC both improve by >3 percentage points in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved 4.7 points, RETAIL_REC improved 2.8 points from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed -70%, or GROCERY_PHARM reverses by more than 2 points in week t+1w.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained four-week trend of RETAIL_REC improvement (from -90.3% to -82.9%, a 7.4 point recovery) indicates momentum in consumer confidence independent of any single driver. This trend momentum continues, producing further RETAIL_REC gains over the next four weeks if the rate of improvement remains positive.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved 7.4 percentage points over four weeks from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC week-on-week improvement rate falls to zero or becomes negative in week t+1w, or RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed -75%.
